## Frozen literals for the deleted-filename sweep (recorded per AC5)

Pre-sweep of all 10 basenames at `bd793558957`, whole tree, before any edit.

**The plan's Testing section understates the live set.** It asserts "the live set is exactly the one allowlist row above and nothing else." Measured, there are **5** hits outside `.test_durations`, not 1:

| Path | Hits | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt:14` | 1 | **live** — the row this story removes (AC4) |
| `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T4.eval.yaml:99,:298` | 2 | **frozen** — recorded here |
| `evals/plan-review-gate/fixtures/eval_specs/plan-review-T9.eval.yaml:173,:515` | 2 | **frozen** — recorded here |

All 4 eval hits name `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` in the same captured sentence: "the pre-existing `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py` continues to prove the checker's detection." That text is a historical plan description frozen as **input** to the plan-review eval harness, with run outputs recorded against it under `evals/plan-review-gate/runs/`. Editing the input would desynchronize it from those recorded outputs and silently change what the eval measures. It is prose inside a YAML string, not a resolvable path, so nothing imports or collects it. Same class as `.test_durations`: frozen, generated-against, not a code reference. **Leave all 4; AC5's exclusion clause now covers them.**

AC5 therefore passes at exactly 1 live hit, which AC4 removes.

### Substring hazard: checked, absent here

Sibling story `19c3` has an AC1 that cannot pass because `test_registry_heldout.py` is a substring of `test_attest_registry_heldout.py`, so its unanchored `git grep -F` returns permanent false hits. **This directory is clean.** For all 10 basenames, unanchored `git grep -F` and word-anchored `git grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])<basename>"` return identical counts, so no basename here matches inside a longer one. AC5's `-F` form is sound as written and needs no amendment.

### Pair census confirms the plan

Exactly **10** paired `_heldout.py` modules directly under `tests/scripts/`, plus exactly **1** unpaired (`test_canary_status_refs_heldout.py`, out of scope per Scope and AC1). Both numbers match the plan. The allowlist row cited at `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt:14` resolves exactly, pinned at 30.

## Context / Problem
10 modules directly under `tests/scripts/` have a `<name>_heldout.py` twin. Once both oracles have been reviewed the split only doubles module count, duplicates identical helper definitions, and makes every rename touch two files. Across these 10 pairs no test-function name collides; 7 pairs carry helper/fixture/class/const definitions with differing bodies (this directory has the densest rename set) and every other colliding definition is identical. Three of the held-out twins — `test_check_adr_numbers_heldout.py`, `test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py`, `test_check_config_reads_heldout.py` — lose their real-tree and CI-wiring tests in the test-suite epic's single-owner story (E10a-S3, aware-obvious-sphinx); this story merges the post-E10a-S3 remainder of those three modules. The pair list with per-pair rename sets, filtered from enumeration (2) of the test-suite epic's first comment, is itemised in this ticket's first comment. Cites re-measured on origin/main ce5795c6a5c (2026-10-31): the 10 pairs, the absence of any colliding test name, the 7 differing-definition pairs and the 13 renames were each re-counted from `git ls-tree origin/main` and an AST diff of every pair, not sampled; all four numbers were unchanged from the earlier 7927904a0 measurement.

## Approach
Directory: `tests/scripts/` — 10 pairs; 13 definition renames spread over 7 pairs — `_closed_bug` (test_backfill_bug_class), `_repo_with_commits` (test_backfill_complexity_clone), `mod`/`FakeRunner`/`alert_env` (test_canary_bridge), `gate`/`_SCRIPT`/`_adr` (test_check_adr_numbers), `_root` (test_check_config_ownership), `gate`/`_tree`/`_SCRIPT` (test_check_config_reads), `_mod` (test_normalize_ci_conclusion_port). For each pair: `cat` the held-out module into the base under a `# ── held-out oracles (merged from <name>_heldout.py) ──` divider; keep the base module docstring and append the held-out docstring's "what it proves" paragraph; dedupe identical definitions (`pytestmark` counts here — keep the base copy); rename differing definitions and repoint their callers; `git rm` the held-out file. Rename rule: suffix the HELD-OUT definition `_heldout` (e.g. `_load_heldout`, `_SCRIPT_HELDOUT` for a constant, `gate_heldout` for a fixture) and repoint its callers; keep the base copy of identical definitions. `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_red_proof.py` (the only `*_red_proof.py`) is untouched and stays a separate module; `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads.py` and its twin cite bug 2c58-e710-275e-4ff7, and that docstring stays the base docstring. No test body changes.

**Repoint the vocabulary allowlist (measured, not hypothetical).** `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` pins an exact occurrence count per path; `scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` rejects drift in either direction (`actual != allowance.count`, line 318) and errors outright on a pinned path that no longer exists (line 151). Two of its rows are this story's pair: `tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria.py` pinned at 6 and `tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria_heldout.py` pinned at 30. Merging that pair therefore requires deleting the twin's row and re-pinning the base row to its measured post-merge count (36 unless the dedupe drops occurrences — re-count, never assume). Omitting this fails `make lint`, which runs the gate (`Makefile:366`), so it is a commit-time blocker rather than a late one.

## Scope
In scope: the 10 base modules under `tests/scripts/` named in the first comment and their 10 `_heldout` twins. Out of scope: `tests/scripts/test_check_config_reads_red_proof.py`, the one unpaired `tests/scripts/` held-out module still present, `test_canary_status_refs_heldout.py` (renamed in S5; the other three this ticket once listed have already gone), the pairs of S1, S2 and S3, every `scripts/check_*.py`, the `Makefile`, every file under `src/`, and any test body change.

## Testing
**Whole-tree deleted-filename sweep, before `make test`.** For each of the 10 removed `_heldout.py` basenames, `git grep -F <basename>` over the whole tree and classify every hit as a live reference (fix), stale prose (fix), or a frozen pre-fix literal (leave, and record it on this ticket). Sweeping only the merged pair is demonstrably insufficient: sibling story 361f-0a5c-bd12-463b broke four guard modules it never edited — a `parametrize` list, a nested-pytest node id, an AST-scan target path and a vocabulary allowlist entry — and its earlier pair-scoped run passed because a merged module never cites a sibling's path. Measured for this directory, the live set is exactly the one allowlist row above and nothing else. `.test_durations` hits are excluded: it is a pytest-split sharding profile, tolerant of stale keys and exempt from the vocabulary gate, confirmed by 361f deleting 39 modules keyed in it with no resulting failure. Then `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` exits 0.

Per pair: `pytest --collect-only -q <base> <heldout>` before and `pytest --collect-only -q <base>` after — counts equal (both recorded on this ticket; the before count for the three `test_check_*` pairs is taken after E10a-S3 landed); `pytest <base>` green. `make test` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zero paired twins remain in this directory: for each of the 10 pairs `git ls-files tests/scripts/<base>_heldout.py` prints nothing (the single unpaired `_heldout` module here, `test_canary_status_refs_heldout.py`, is untouched and renamed in S5).
- [ ] Per-pair node counts reconcile: each merged base collects exactly the sum of the two prior counts, from the before/after `pytest --collect-only -q` runs recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **exits 0** — this story introduces no unadmitted mechanism. **AMENDED 2026-10-31 — the original `shows new=0` form is unmeetable.** `new=N` counts marker-ADMITTED entries as well as unadmitted ones, so a clean tree at current main already reports a nonzero `new` and exits 0. No implementation of this story could drive that counter to 0, so the criterion would fail at the end regardless of the work. Exit 0 is the gate's real pass signal, which is the property this AC means to assert. Root cause filed as bug `6f24-3d47-b251-4905`, now fixed in `AGENTS.md` and `rebar explain plan`. No `tests/_*.py` helper, check script, workflow step, nor autouse fixture is added here.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` **exits 0**, with the `tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria_heldout.py` row removed from `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` and the surviving `tests/scripts/test_migrate_success_criteria.py` row re-pinned to its measured post-merge count.
- [ ] No deleted filename is still referenced: for each of the 10 removed `_heldout.py` basenames, `git grep -F <basename>` returns no hit outside `.test_durations` and any frozen pre-fix literal explicitly recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] `make verify` green.
